messages:
jon (AE): Elysium requested a short perf validation: steady 100 qps chat (512 seq), 4 short microbursts up to 700 qps, and a comparison between redwood-7b-fp32 and redwood-7b-4bit. They want reproducible CI commands, a compact SLO table, and a short security note on prompt retention.

tess (SRE): Plan: 15m warm, 30m steady @100 qps, bursts: 2m@300, 2m@500, 4m@700, 6m cooldown. Collect p50/p95/p99/p99.9, gpu slice util, batch size dist, kv cache hit. Tag runs with customer=elysium env=bench.

priya (SE): Use seq_in 128 / seq_out 384 -> 512. Recommend run both warm and cold cache for 4bit to show variance. Add routing fallback to fp32 during sustained p95 > 400ms for >10s.

sam (Solutions Eng): Quick cost sketch: assume avg output 60 tok/resp. Token math: 100 * 60 = 6k tok/s steady. Example list-rate numbers: fp32 $0.0000010/token, 4bit $0.00000036/token. I'll produce a short cost appendix after runs.

ci-bot: job elysium-bench-v1 queued (id: ci-elysium-2025-09-10)

tess (SRE): Pasteable CI command to give the customer:
```bash
./tools/bench_runner \
  --profile profiles/elysium_multi_sla.json \
  --model redwood-7b-4bit \
  --duration 3600 \
  --output gs://redwood-temp/elysium/run-4bit.json \
  --meta "customer=elysium,run=multi-sla" \
  --redact-prompts true
```
Redact flag hashes inputs; we keep only hashes + token counts for compliance.

priya (SE): Also note: if they require HSM/KMS proofs recommend Dedicated or Private. Hosted runs use encrypted buckets with limited share windows; we can provide deletion logs.

tess (SRE): interim: steady 30m @100qps complete on 4bit. p95 135ms, p99 320ms, p99.9 650ms, gpu_util 60%, batch median 8, no drops. Partial results uploaded: gs://redwood-temp/elysium/interim-4bit.json

jon (AE): Good. Run fp32 next and then the bursts. Need writeup and cost appendix for Thursday sync.

tess (SRE): final: all runs complete. Topline: 4bit warm steady p95 140ms, burst@700 p95 500ms, burst@700 p99.9 1.1s. fp32 warm steady p95 90ms, burst@700 p95 240ms, burst@700 p99.9 680ms. Observed cost delta ~3.2x fp32 vs 4bit. Artifacts and redact manifest uploaded to gs://redwood-temp/elysium/final/.

sam (Solutions Eng): Recommendation: If Elysium needs tight tail SLAs choose fp32 on Dedicated for primary traffic and use 4bit for cost-sensitive steady traffic with fallback. If they can commit to pre-warming cache, 4bit looks very cost-effective. I'll attach the cost appendix with hosted vs commit scenarios.

priya (SE): I'll draft the 1-pager (TL;DR, test config, p95/p99/p99.9 table, heatmap, recommendation) and share a draft link. Need final numbers inserted by EOD.

jon (AE): Thanks team. Action items: tess upload final profiles + redact proof, priya draft writeup, sam finalize cost appendix, jon prepare customer deck. Meeting Thursday 2pm PT. :thumbsup:
